entries.title: Numbers 11:1
segments: The fire of the Lord; a miraculous fire proceeding from Jehovah's presence.  Compare

. 
 
Discontentment with the dealings of God is unwise and wicked.  Those who indulge in it provoke him, and expose themselves to his wrath.

entries.title: Numbers 11:2
segments: The wicked are more indebted to the righteous than they are apt to imagine, and in their distresses they often feel this, and look to them for help.

entries.title: Numbers 11:3
segments: Taberah; a burning.

entries.title: Numbers 11:4
segments: Mixed multitude;
Fell a lusting; impatiently desired other kinds of food.

entries.title: Numbers 11:6
segments:
Our soul is dried away; we languish and are suffering for want of other food. 
 
We are apt to depreciate and undervalue the blessings we have, and to magnify and overrate those which we desire.

entries.title: Numbers 11:7
segments:
As coriander-seed; a small round seed. 
 
  Bdellium; according to some, the pearl; according to others, a gummy secretion of a yellowish-white color.

entries.title: Numbers 11:11
segments: The best of men are but partly sanctified; and not unfrequently in their hearts, and sometimes in words, they find fault with God.

entries.title: Numbers 11:15
segments:
Out of hand; at once, now. 
 
Those who kill themselves, or ask God or men to kill them, are not in a proper state to die.  Did they feel right, whatever their trials, they would say, All the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.  Not my will, but thine be done.

entries.title: Numbers 11:17
segments:
Put it upon them; furnish them with the special influences of my Spirit, as I have furnished thee, to fit them for their work. 
 
God is often kind and gracious in withholding from them what they need. If he calls them to great and difficult services, they have no reason to complain or to despond; if they trust in him he will provide for them, that as their duties are, their ability may also be.

entries.title: Numbers 11:18
segments: Sanctify yourselves; by the customary rites,
.  These signified and demanded of the people inward purification.

entries.title: Numbers 11:20
segments:
Come out at your nostrils; they would eat flesh till they were not only satisfied, but made sick by it and loathed it. 
 
What people impatiently and wickedly desire, God sometimes suffers them to have, and to abuse to their ruin.

entries.title: Numbers 11:23
segments:
Waxed short; is God unable to do what he has promised? 
 
It needs stronger faith than good men often have, or without the influences of the Holy Spirit would ever have, to believe that God will do all that he has promised.

entries.title: Numbers 11:25
segments: Prophesied; prophecy is here used in the widest sense, as often in the New Testament, to denote all religious discourse delivered under immediate inspiration.  Compare
.  In the same sense it is also employed elsewhere in the Old Testament.

entries.title: Numbers 11:28
segments: Forbid them; Joshua seems to have thought that, in remaining behind, they had been guilty of disrespect towards Moses.  But Moses rejoiced in every gift of God's Spirit, though some irregularity might be connected with it.  Compare

entries.title: Numbers 11:29
segments: It is natural for men to envy others on account of the blessings which God gives them; but divine grace teaches us to rejoice in the blessings of others, and to desire that, if consistent, such blessings may be given to all.

entries.title: Numbers 11:31
segments:
From the sea; that it, from Africa beyond the Red sea, where quails are found at the present day in prodigious numbers. 
 
  Two cubits high; that is, in heaps about two cubits high.

entries.title: Numbers 11:32
segments: Ten homers; an ephah is estimated to have contained about one and one-twelfth bushels, and a homer was ten ephahs.  We are not, however, to understand ten homers for each individual, but rather, for each head of a household.  Some propose to render "ten heaps," as the word is elsewhere used,

; but the sacred writer plainly means to indicate a definite quantity.  This immense provision showed not only the abundance of the quails, but also the inordinate lust for which God punished the people.

entries.title: Numbers 11:33
segments: God may in wrath give men what they desire, to show them and others the wickedness and folly of wishing to have their own way, and refusing to be guided and governed by him.

entries.title: Numbers 11:34
segments:
Kibroth-hattaavah; that is, the graves of lust. 
 
Lust, and the use of things lusted after, are plagues which have opened and filled many graves.

entries.title: Numbers 11:35
segments: Hazeroth; a place still farther on the way towards Canaan.
